transcript: When we talk about advances in injectable fillers, we tend to focus on what happens when the product is injected. But something that's equally important that happens long before the filler ever reaches the patient, it really happens during the manufacturing process. Evelise is a collection of hyaluronic acid injectables made using something called cold-ex technology. That temperature actually plays in preserving the hyaluronic acid molecule. Hyaluronic acid, otherwise known as HA, is a molecule that occurs naturally within our skin and all our tissues, connective tissue. And one of its important properties is its ability to bind water. But hyaluronic acid is also sensitive to the way it's processed. This is where the key important thing is. Traditional filler manufacturing can involve heat during the cross-linking process and heat can contribute to the breakdown or sort of what we call fragmentation of that hyaluronic acid chains. Cold-ex technology takes really a different approach. It uses near freezing temperature during the manufacturing process. The goal is a filler that's designed to perform better within the treatment area while looking and feeling natural. And within the Evelise collection, we can currently have Evelise form, which has a little more structure. Evelise smooth, which is therefore smoother, and both are made using cold-ex technology. And they have really different, what we call viscoelastic properties, different viscosities. And this way allows us to select a product that's based on the treatment goal. And for me, as a physician and an artist, this is where science really becomes clinically relevant. We're not simply looking at how much volume a filler can create. We're thinking more about the properties of the gel, how it behaves within a dynamic area of the face, and ultimately how that translates into the result we see and feel. Patients today are increasingly telling me the same thing. They want natural results. They don't want to look like they've had filler. They want to remain and maintain their expression. They want to maintain their individuality. They don't want to look different. And that's what makes the science behind cold-ex technology really interesting to me and useful. So it's an innovation to me that really begins at the molecular and manufacturing level. It's designed around something very simple, a natural-looking and a natural-feeling result.

transcript: La crème solaire cause le cancer. Attention, c'est un mythe. Je suis chimiste et je vous explique. C'est vrai que des études ont observé que l'utilisation de crème solaire était associée à une augmentation des risques de cancer de la peau. Donc on pourrait regarder ça et se dire 1 plus ça, un égal, 2. Si les gens qui utilisent la crème solaire ont plus de cancer de la peau, ça doit bien vouloir dire que c'est la crème solaire qui cause le cancer. Mais attention, corrélation ne veut pas dire causalité. Je vous donne un exemple. Durant l'été, il y a plus de gens qui mangent de crème glacée et il y a aussi plus de cas de noyade. Mais on pourrait pas dire que c'est la crème glacée qui cause ces noyades, c'est simplement une corrélation. Et c'est la même chose avec la crème solaire. C'est pas elle qui est responsable de la hausse des cas de cancer, mais plutôt le paradoxe de la crème solaire. Comme l'explique le docteur Litvinov, les gens qui s'exposent le plus au soleil ont aussi tendance à utiliser plus de crème solaire, mais il ne l'applique pas en quantité suffisante et n'en réapplique pas assez souvent, ce qui leur procure un faux sentiment de sécurité. Et il y a aussi beaucoup de gens qui utilisent la crème solaire comme une permission pour aller se faire bronzer au soleil. Les utilisateurs de crème solaire se retrouvent donc plus exposés au rayon UV du soleil qui, eux, sont cancerigènes. Et c'est ce qui expliquerait la hausse des cas de cancer de la peau chez ces personnes. Alors non seulement la crème solaire ne cause pas le cancer, on sait aussi que c'est un outil de prévention efficace contre les cancers de la peau à condition qu'elle soit bien utilisée. Sachant qu'un seul coup de soleil dans l'enfant sous l'adolescence peut plus que doubler les risques de développer un mélanome plus tard dans la vie, et bien on sait que se protéger adéquatement du soleil à l'aide de la crème solaire et d'autres mesures de protection peut significativement réduire les risques de développer un cancer de la peau. Allez suivre la campagne ensemble contre la désinformation de la science d'abord pour qu'ensemble on mette fin à ces mythes dangereux.

creator: DrAlexisStephens
title: Cosmetic Procedures for Skin of Color
caption:
Healthy, radiant skin is the most universally desired human feature regardless of skin tone. Structural and biological differences in melanin-rich skin warrant a more conservative approach to cosmetic and skin rejuvenation procedures. This sometimes requires using different devices from those with fair skin for the best and safest outcomes. Most adverse events from cosmetic procedures in melanin-rich skin occur from overaggressive treatments or unsafe techniques/devices for skin of color.

title: Melasma Treatment Takes Strategy
caption: Melasma is not a one-product problem. Sunscreen, pigment control, procedures, triggers, and maintenance all matter, especially during high-UV months.
